BY THE COURT

JUDGMENT

[
1
]

The appellant essentially pleads that the Superior Court was
wrong, first in condemning her in her capacity as the administrator of her
mother’s property, second in rejecting her claim for harassment and loss of
income, and, third, in declaring her a vexatious litigant.

[
2
]

All these arguments merely raise questions of fact or mixed
questions of fact and law. In order to succeed, the appellant has the burden to
show one or more palpable and dominant errors in the judgment appealed from (
Housen
v. Nikolaisen,
2002 SCC 33 (CanLII)
, [2002] 2 S.C.R. 235).

[
3
]

After a thorough analysis, we are all of the opinion that the
appellant has failed to overcome the burden incumbent on her, thus preventing
this Court from intervening in any fashion whatsoever.

FOR THESE REASONS,

[
4
]

The appeal is
DISMISSED
, with costs.

FRANÇOIS PELLETIER, J.A.

PIERRETTE RAYLE, J.A.

JACQUES DUFRESNE, J.A.
